string-array.name: step_by_step_puzzles
string-array.item: Shark|Lives in water.|Has an exceptionally developed sense of smell.|Some species can grow several metres long.|Has multiple rows of sharp teeth.|Known for having to swim continuously.|Featured in the famous movie "Jaws".|Belongs to the group of predatory fish.

Nikola Tesla|Born in the nineteenth century.|Held over three hundred patents worldwide.|Worked extensively in the United States.|His famous experimental station was in Colorado Springs.|The SI unit of magnetic flux density is named after him.|Best known for developing alternating current (AC).|Renowned electrical engineer and inventor of Serbian descent.

Paris|A river flows through it.|Has a population of over two million people.|Known as the City of Light.|Home to the famous Louvre Museum.|Recognized by the Notre-Dame Cathedral.|Famous for the Eiffel Tower.|Capital city of France.

Moon|Does not emit its own light.|Lacks an atmosphere and liquid surface water.|Exerts gravitational pull creating tides on Earth.|Its surface features numerous craters and maria.|Humans first set foot on it in 1969.|Cycles through phases including new, crescent and full.|Earth\'s only permanent natural satellite.

Pizza|Baked at very high temperatures.|Typically round and sliced into triangles.|Base made of fermented wheat dough.|Traditionally baked in a wood-fired oven.|A popular classic variety is called Margherita.|Originated in Naples, Italy.|World-famous Italian dish topped with tomato sauce and cheese.

Titanic|Constructed in a shipyard in Belfast.|Departed from the port of Southampton.|Widely believed to be unsinkable.|Featured four iconic steam funnels.|Sank after colliding with an iceberg in April 1912.|Inspired James Cameron\'s multi-Oscar winning 1997 film.|Famous British passenger ocean liner that sank on its maiden voyage.

Tennis|Played either in singles or doubles format.|Played on grass, clay or hard court surfaces.|Points are scored as 15, 30, and 40.|Service is delivered over the net into the diagonal service box.|The four major tournaments are called Grand Slams.|Played with stringed rackets and a yellow felt ball.|Sport known for Wimbledon and Grand Slam tournaments.

Guitar|Can be acoustic, classical or electric.|Features a hollow or solid body and a fretted neck.|Frets along the fingerboard determine the pitch.|Often played using fingertips or a plectrum (pick).|Standard model features six strings.|Core rhythm and lead instrument in rock and pop music.|Popular fretted stringed musical instrument.

Sun|Composed predominantly of hydrogen and helium.|Energy is generated by nuclear fusion in its core.|Light from it takes about eight minutes to reach Earth.|Primary source of light and heat for our solar system.|All planets in our system revolve around it.|Shines brightly in the sky during daytime.|The star at the centre of our Solar System.

Coffee|Cultivated primarily in tropical equatorial regions.|Two most common commercial species are Arabica and Robusta.|Beans are dried, roasted and ground.|Contains the natural stimulant alkaloid caffeine.|Popular styles include espresso, cappuccino and latte.|Commonly consumed in the morning to increase alertness.|Brewed caffeinated beverage made from roasted beans.

Rome|Located along the Tiber River.|Known universally as the Eternal City.|Historically built upon seven hills.|Encompasses the independent city-state of the Vatican.|Home to the ancient amphitheatre Colosseum.|Former capital of a mighty ancient classical empire.|Capital city of Italy.

Wolf|Possesses keen senses of hearing and smell.|Lives and hunts cooperatively in a pack.|Dominant breeding leaders are known as the alpha pair.|Famous for vocal communication by howling.|Classic antagonist in fairy tales like Little Red Riding Hood.|Direct wild ancestor of the domestic dog.|Largest wild member of the Canidae (dog) family.

Telephone|Patented in the second half of the nineteenth century.|Connects people across vast distances.|Early models featured a rotating rotary dial.|Historically tethered by a cord to a wall socket.|Nowadays predominantly portable touchscreen smartphones.|Invention widely credited to Alexander Graham Bell.|Telecommunication device used for transmitting sound and voice.

Basketball|Invented by James Naismith in the United States.|Originally played using peach baskets as targets.|Played with an orange bouncy ball.|Each team fields five active players on the court.|Shots made from beyond the arc count for three points.|Objective is to shoot the ball through an elevated hoop with a net.|Globally popular indoor team sport.

Chess|Traced back to an ancient Indian game called chaturanga.|Played on a board composed of sixty-four checkered squares.|Board and pieces are divided into light and dark (white and black).|Each player commands sixteen pieces at the start.|Pieces include pawns, knights, bishops, rooks, and a queen.|The game is won by checkmating the opponent\'s king.|Classic abstract strategy board game for two players.

Mona Lisa|Painted in oil on a white poplar wood panel.|Depicts a seated woman with an enigmatic and subtle smile.|Celebrated masterpiece of Italian Renaissance art.|Housed behind bulletproof glass in the Louvre Museum in Paris.|Also widely known by the Italian title La Gioconda.|Painted by polymath Leonardo da Vinci.|The world\'s most famous portrait painting.

Car|First modern practical model was built by Karl Benz.|Operated using a steering wheel, accelerator and brakes.|Equipped with pneumatic rubber tyres.|Body styles include sedan, hatchback, estate and SUV.|Can be powered by internal combustion, hybrid or electric motor.|Typically runs on four wheels and carries passengers.|Motorized road vehicle for personal transport.

London|Located on the banks of the River Thames.|Famous for iconic red double-decker buses and black cabs.|Home to the Palace of Westminster and Tower Bridge.|Distinguished by the famous Elizabeth Tower bell known as Big Ben.|Official residence of the British monarch at Buckingham Palace.|Located on the island of Great Britain.|Capital city of the United Kingdom and England.

Bee|Lives in a highly organized colony or society.|Colony consists of a single queen, female workers, and male drones.|Plays a vital ecological role in pollinating flowering plants.|Constructs hexagonal beeswax combs inside hives.|Female workers possess a venomous stinger.|Collects nectar and pollen from blossoms.|Flying insect famous for producing sweet honey.

Chocolate|Raw ingredient is harvested from the cacao tree.|Ancient Maya and Aztecs consumed it as a frothy bitter drink.|Common varieties include dark, milk, and white.|Main components are cocoa solids and cocoa butter.|Frequently combined with roasted hazelnuts, almonds or caramel.|Globally adored confectionery sweet treat.|Sweet confection that melts at body temperature.

Football|Played on a rectangular grass pitch with two goal nets.|Each team fields eleven players during a match.|Only the goalkeeper may handle the ball inside the penalty area.|Standard match consists of two halves of forty-five minutes.|The premier global tournament is the FIFA World Cup.|Played by kicking and passing a spherical ball.|The most popular team sport in the world.

Book|Can have a soft paperback or hard cover binding.|Consists of printed pages fastened together along one side.|Can be a novel, textbook, encyclopedia or poetry collection.|Features a title, author, table of contents and page numbers.|Stored on shelves in libraries and bookstores.|Read for knowledge, education, storytelling or entertainment.|Bound written or printed work.

Airplane|First controlled powered flight was made by the Wright brothers.|Features fixed wings that generate aerodynamic lift.|Takes off and lands on paved airport runways.|Operated from a cockpit by licensed pilots.|Can be commercial passenger, cargo, or military.|Powered by jet turbines or propeller engines.|Heavier-than-air powered flying aircraft.

Volcano|Forms along ruptures and boundaries of tectonic plates.|Often topped with a circular crater or caldera.|Famous historical examples include Vesuvius, Etna, and Mount Fuji.|Can be classified as active, dormant, or extinct.|Eruptions spew ash, rock fragments, steam and toxic gases.|Molten rock known as magma erupts onto the surface as lava.|Rupture or geological vent in the crust of a planetary-mass object.

Leonardo da Vinci|Lived and worked during the Italian Renaissance.|Kept private notebooks written in reverse mirror-image script.|Designed visionary conceptual sketches of flying machines and parachutes.|Painted the monumental mural "The Last Supper".|Created the iconic anatomical drawing "Vitruvian Man".|Painted the world\'s most famous portrait "Mona Lisa".|Archetypal Renaissance polymath, master painter and inventor.
